audit_items.proof_trace: mint_ctokens computes mint_amount = int_div(collateral_amount, exchange_rate()) with no assertion that mint_amount > 0; when exchange_rate > collateral_amount (which occurs naturally after interest accrual raises debt while total_supply stays fixed), int_div truncates to 0, causing coins to enter the reserve via deposit_underlying while 0 ctokens are minted. The developer-acknowledged TODO at L159 confirms awareness of this rounding gap. Classic donation-inflation is blocked by Sui Move's object model, but interest-driven rate growth is sufficient to violate the second assertion (ctokens_minted2 > 0).
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker deposits 1 unit as the first depositor (gets 1 cToken at 1:1 rate), borrows against that collateral so interest accrues over time and exchange_rate rises above 1; a victim then deposits 1 unit, receives 0 ctokens (int_div(1, >1.0) = 0), and their coins silently inflate the reserve. The attacker later redeems their 1 cToken to capture the victim's deposited funds.
